findings.passage: “Let’s pick some low-hanging fruit and some things that will really benefit our elections, make them more secure and uphold the integrity of our elections,” Branscum said.
findings.note: Quoted by WKMS (Kentucky Public Radio, published 2021-02-25) on the day the House elections committee passed HB 574, his omnibus elections bill. The story does not say he was speaking of voter ID; it covers absentee rules, vote centers and early voting.

findings.passage: I have and continue to believe that elections are the fabric of our democracy and it is critical that we uphold the security and integrity of the election process.
findings.note: His end-of-session legislative update (posted on a local radio station's news page after the 2022 session ended in mid-April), under the heading 'Election Security'. He then lists what HB 564 does: in-person absentee voting, tamper-resistant seals, a ban on connecting voting equipment to the internet, and a risk-limiting audit pilot. No mention of voter ID.
